grade.primary_choice: Stay on .NET isolated with startup tuning; move this app to Flex Consumption with 1–2 always-ready instances, raised before sale days
unsupported_claims: AKS with KEDA 'extra cost is close to zero' is too glib, even with the spare-capacity caveat
grade.notes: This is a strong answer. It correctly blames platform and scale-out delays rather than the language, and it recommends Flex always-ready plus .NET isolated tuning, measurement, provider-throttling checks and the November 2026 in-process deadline, with Native AOT properly hedged. Its one gap is that it never says a steady few messages per minute probably already keeps one instance warm, and it barely mentions a lean deployment package.
